reason: Holding the carry book unchanged after limited web research (3 searches, 1 fetch). A mid-November report (Mitrade, citing CME FedWatch as of Nov 12) put the odds of a hike at the Dec 9 FOMC at 100%, after a strong October payrolls print and hot inflation; Gov. Waller floated a 50bp move. I found no FedWatch reading after mid-November. That tightening path is exactly what this mandate is built for: JAAA (50%) and ICLO (16%) are AAA CLO floaters whose coupons reset upward with each hike while engine cash stays at 4%. Both are up about 0.8% with very low volatility and sit far from their 8% stops. AMLP (-3.05%) and SPYI (-3.29%) are the drags. Undated reports of US-Iran peace efforts easing oil-supply fears may be weighing on energy, but AMLP is a fee-based midstream inflation hedge with a 15% stop and a ~7%+ distribution yield, so a 3% drawdown does not break the thesis. SPYI's covered-call income is intact after an equity rebound week, with its 12% stop well away. I could not find current CLO spread data or a late-November oil close. Nothing I did find argues for rotating, and a full replacement would cost real basis points against a carry book whose edge is the accrual itself. Stops are unchanged.
